Question:
Some Heck cattle are artificially selected.
Predicates:
BreedingBack(x) ::: x is a form of artificial selection by deliberate selective breeding.
HeckCattle(x) ::: x is Heck cattle.
BredBackIn(x, y) ::: x was bred-back in year y.
Resemble(x, y) ::: x resembles y.
Extinct(y) ::: y is extinct.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Premises:
BreedingBack(heckCattle) ∧ BredBackIn(heckCattle, 1920s) ∧ HeckCattle(heckCattle) ∧ Animal(heckCattle) ::: Heck cattle were bred-back in the 1920s to resemble the aurochs, and Heck cattle are animals.
Aurochs(x) ∧ Animal(x) ::: Aurochs are animals.
∃x (Animal(x) ∧ Resemble(x, extinctAnimal)) ::: Some animals to be bred-back resemble animals that are extinct.
Conclusion:
∃x (HeckCattle(x) ∧ ArtificiallySelected(x)) ::: Some Heck cattle are artificially selected.
